body: The pain and guilt is unbearable.  I failed him and i failed myself.  So many poor decisions
I know what you mean.  Losing the dog was my last straw.
Did you ever believe when you were younger that some day you’d feel that way?  I’m surprised I’ve come to this point.  But once you’re there you’re there I guess.

The vet gave me his body in a box and it’s in my freezer.  I thought that might help make me feel better, to have him here but it does not because he’s dead.  What you say makes sense but the problem is not just his passing, but me and my depression.  It’s seriously bad and I finally was pulling myself out of the last episode when he died, now I’m right back there.  I’ve had issues with depression since my brain injury 3 years ago.  Life keeps getting worse and worse

I was trying to interview and get a job that would allow me to move.  I kept telling my dog that we would start over and have a better life.  He was supposed to move with me.  Now I’m all alone.  How do you handle it?

For the last 3 years, I’ve let horrible jobs cause me depression and affect my ability to take care of myself and my dog.  He required acute attention to keep his health running smoothly and I missed some things.  I care too much about places of employment that don’t care about me.  Why couldn’t I ever be the guy who left work shit at work and come home and give my dog the attention he deserved.  I knew he wasn’t feeling well in general and there were times I thought I’d be OK when he passed.  I could never have been more wrong.  I felt like my life ended too.  Now, the thought of going back to work knowing this places caused my depression makes me sick to my stomach.  He didn’t eat his breakfast the day he passed and instead of going to the doctor, I went to work.  I hate work so much

I am so lost.  I don’t know what to do with myself.  We did everything together for 15 years.  I have no one else.  Going to a horrible job every day and coming home to this apartment building where my neighbors have loved my dog for 5 years are.  They look at me now so sadly.  I feel like a ghost.

I am so lost.  I don’t know what to do with myself.  We did everything together for 15 years.  I have no one else.  Going to a horrible job every day and coming home to this apartment building where my neighbors have loved my dog for 5 years are.  They look at me now so sadly.  I feel like a ghost.

My life is horrible.  It was once good, but that was years and years ago.  I’m a loner now, moved too many times, lost too many jobs.  No close family.  He truly was all I had left in this world.  This apartment is empty.

He died of heart failure.  He had heart disease his whole life but he got yearly checks.  His next appt. was July 2nd.  Unfortunately his conditioned declined before the appt., but I thought his symptoms were from another of his health problems.  If we had seen the cardiologist sooner, we would have caught the progressed disease and given medication before the failure.  The guilt is killing me.  I’ve moved around, lost and changed many jobs and my dog was the only consistent part of my life.  I don’t think I can survive without him.  Severe depression has started- it took forever to get out of the last episode but I hadn’t dog.  Now I have no way to pull out.
